---
# flutter_agent_harness

[![CI](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![pub package](https://img.shields.io/pub/v/flutter_agent_harness.svg)](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_agent_harness)
[![CRAP max 12.0 — measured whole-tree](https://img.shields.io/badge/CRAP%20max-12.0-brightgreen)](https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart)
[![CRAP app max 30.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/CRAP%20app-30.0-yellow)](https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart)
[![coverage ≥ 80%](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-%E2%89%A5%2093%25-brightgreen)](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness)

Cross-platform AI agent harness for Dart and Flutter — streaming provider
adapters, an agent loop with native tool calling, JSONL session persistence,
context compaction, and a pi-like terminal coding agent (`fa`). Architecture
ported from [pi-mono](https://github.com/badlogicgames/pi-mono)
(`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), with a pure-Dart core that runs on the
VM, Flutter desktop/mobile, and web.

**[fa1.dev](https://fa1.dev)** — the project website: a live in-browser
demo of the full agent (sandboxed shell, git, interpreters — your key
stays in page memory), the [iOS public
beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/En1eC9UK) on TestFlight, the
[macOS app](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/latest),
and the CLI installer below.

## Design contract

- **Pure Dart core.** No `dart:io`, no Flutter imports in `lib/` — platform
  capabilities live behind abstractions (`ExecutionEnv`); the IO
  implementation is a separate entry point (`lib/io.dart`), so the core
  compiles for web.
- **Errors-as-events.** Providers never throw: network failures, 429s,
  malformed SSE — everything arrives as an `error` event with a stop
  reason. The agent loop never dies on a dropped connection.
- **Streaming-first, partial-first.** `Stream<AgentEvent>` everywhere;
  every delta event carries the live partial message.
- **Native tool calling** per provider (OpenAI `tools`, Anthropic
  `tool_use`, Google `functionCalling`). Prompt-based calling exists only
  as an opt-in adapter for chat-only runtimes.
- **Token accounting inline**, overflow detection per provider, and
  token-based (never message-count-based) context management.
- **Cancellation everywhere** via `CancelToken` — providers, loop, tools.

## What's inside

- **Agent core** (`lib/src/`): the async agent loop, steering + follow-up
  message queues (inject input mid-run), hooks (`beforeToolCall`,
  `afterToolCall`, `transformContext`, `prepareNextTurn`), model roles
  (`default`/`smol`/`slow`/`plan`) with fallback chains, API-key rotation,
  429 mid-turn take-over, and stream watchdogs (connect + idle timeouts
  with config overrides).
- **Providers**: openai-completions (covers OpenRouter/DeepSeek/Kimi/Grok/…),
  Anthropic, Google, ChatGPT (Codex OAuth), Copilot (device flow), DIAL,
  MiniMax, z.ai, CodeMie (SSO), Ollama, plus custom providers saved from
  the REPL. One OpenAI-compatible adapter is reused via `baseUrl` swap.
- **Sessions**: append-only JSONL trees (branching, labels, tree
  navigation with branch summaries), token-based auto-compaction with a
  structured summary prompt, and attached-session support (watch a live

content.text:
needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1682: the leaderboard step commits the updated fa-results
    # ledger + regenerated README table back to the repo.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" \
            --json-summary leaderboard-summary.json jobs

      # gh-1682: auto-update the public leaderboard — append the run's
      # result to bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json (idempotent: keyed by
      # dataset version + model, run URLs union) and regenerate the
      # README table. Runs only on a COMPLETE full run (the verdict step
      # succeeded) — smoke/narrowed dispatches (non-empty tasks) never
      # touch the ledger.
      - name: Update leaderboard ledger & table
        if: success() && inputs.tasks == ''
        env:
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python bench/leaderboard/record.py --summary leaderboard-summary.json
          # No --version: render every ledger version + the 4.0 field,
          # so the marked README block is rewritten whole, never shrunk
          # to the dispatch's single family.
          python bench/leaderboard/render.py
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add README.md bench/leaderboard
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "leaderboard: ledger and table already up to date"
          else
            git commit -m "bench: leaderboard ledger update · ${FAMILY} · ${MODEL} (gh-1682)"
            git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
          fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ProgramBench task inventory + shard split for bench-programbench.yml.

Enumerates the official task set from a pinned facebookresearch/ProgramBench
checkout (src/programbench/data/tasks/<org>__<repo>.<sha>/ — the same ids
`programbench eval` matches against <run_dir>/<iid>/), resolves the dispatch
`tasks` selector, and writes the shard matrix to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (or stdout),
the same convention as bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py.

Selector grammar (single `tasks` input, gh-1685):
  ''            full set (~200 instances; the workflow gates this behind
                confirm-full-run — hours of LLM spend)
  smoke         the smoke pair: the two lexicographically first ids
                (deterministic, cheap pipeline proof — AC1)
  lite          a deterministic ~20-instance stride over the sorted set
                (the "full lite-equivalent" AC2 surface)
  <fnmatch,...> comma fnmatch globs, e.g. '__cmatrix*'.* or ffmpeg__*

Output keys: matrix (JSON {include:[{i, tasks, count}]}), count, mode,
total (the FULL inventory size — the summary's dilution guard: a partial
package run's headline divides by the full set, never the selected one).

This script only reads directory names — it never touches docker or the
network, so it runs green in setup on any runner.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LITE_TARGET = 20
SMOKE_SIZE = 2


def _inventory(tasks_dir: Path) -> list[str]:
    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
        raise SystemExit(f"tasks dir not found: {tasks_dir}")
    # Task ids are the per-task dir names; one dir per instance, no nesting.
    ids = sorted(p.name for p in tasks_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
    if not ids:
        raise SystemExit(f"no task instances under {tasks_dir}")
    return ids


def _select(ids: list[str], spec: str) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
    spec = (spec or "").strip()
    if spec == "":
        return ids, "full"
    if spec == "smoke":
        return ids[:SMOKE_SIZE], "smoke"
    if spec == "lite":
        stride = max(1, len(ids) // LITE_TARGET)
        return ids[::stride][:LITE_TARGET], "lite"
    globs = [g.strip() for g in spec.split(",") if g.strip()]
    picked = [i for i in ids if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(i, g) for g in globs)]
    if not picked:
        raise SystemExit(f"no ProgramBench instances match: {spec}")
    return picked, "globs"


def _chunk(tasks: list[str], shards: int) -> list[list[str]]:
    shards = max(1, min(shards, len(tasks) or 1))
    size, extra = divmod(len(tasks), shards)
    out, at = [], 0
    for i in range(shards):
        end = at + size + (1 if i < extra else 0)
        out.append(tasks[at:end])
        at = end
    return out


def _emit(pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
    target = os.environ.get("GITHUB_OUTPUT")
    if target:
        with open(target, "a") as f:
            f.writelines(f"{k}={v}\n" for k, v in pairs)
    else:
        for k, v in pairs:
            print(f"{k}={v}")


def main() -> int:
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if len(args) < 1:
        print("usage: tasks.py <tasks_dir> [--filter SPEC] [--shards N]", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    tasks_dir = Path(args[0])
    flt = ""
    shards = 1
    rest = args[1:]
    for i, a in enumerate(rest):
        if a == "--filter":
            flt = rest[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(rest) else ""
        elif a == "--shards":
            shards = int(rest[i + 1])
    ids = _inventory(tasks_dir)
    picked, mode = _select(ids, flt)
    include = [
        {"i": i, "tasks": " ".join(chunk), "count": len(chunk)}
        for i, chunk in enumerate(_chunk(picked, shards))
        if chunk
    ]
    _emit(
        [
            # Single-line JSON (json.dumps never emits newlines) — same
            # shape split_tasks.py writes, consumed via fromJSON().
            ("matrix", json.dumps({"include": include})),
            ("count", str(len(picked))),
            ("total", str(len(ids))),
            ("mode", mode),
        ]
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml and bench/leaderboard roots — all the
      # bench discovery roots); keep the step bodies in sync with those
      # workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/programbench -v
===
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Three
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface), bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests), and bench/leaderboard (the gh-1682 fetch/record/render
      # suites — fixtures only, no network). Discovering bench/ itself
      # would need __init__.py plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      # Keep the root list in sync with bench-tests.yml.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).

# Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)

> One agent harness, every device. Fa is an open-source coding agent for Dart and
> Flutter with a real tool loop: a sandboxed shell (curl, wget, jq, yq, rg, sed,
> awk, find, xargs, diff/patch, tar/zip), git over HTTP and SSH, python3 and
> sqlite3 running in the browser, secrets redaction, a file browser, and a
> session tree with context compaction. It runs on iOS, Android, web, desktop,
> as a CLI, as a Chrome extension, and as an Outlook add-in.

## Live demo

- [Try Fa in your browser](https://fa1.dev/app/):
  bring your own key (BYOK). Keys are held in memory only — never persisted —
  and calls go directly from the visitor's browser to the LLM provider.

## Install

- iOS / iPadOS / macOS app — App Store (paid release, funds development):
  https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163.
  Free-forever public TestFlight beta:
  https://testflight.apple.com/join/En1eC9UK. Store frames page:
  https://fa1.dev/app-store/. Android: coming soon.
- CLI (macOS, Windows, Linux; requires the Dart SDK, bundled with Flutter):
  `curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh`
  or `dart pub global activate flutter_agent_harness`. Both provide the `fah`
  and `fa` executables. Set a provider API key (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY),
  then run `fah`.
- Flutter demo app from source:
  `git clone https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, then
  `cd flutter_agent_harness/flutter_app && flutter run`.

## Chrome extension

- MV3 extension that hosts the full Fa web app in a side panel; the agent
  runs in the service worker and drives the browser with 32 tools:
  `tabs_open`, `tabs_close`, `tabs_update`, `tabs_query`, `tabs_move`,
  `tabs_group`, `tabs_ungroup`, `tabs_reload`, `tabs_discard`,
  `windows_open`, `windows_update`, `windows_close`, `windows_list`,
  `groups_update`, `groups_close`, `sessions_recent`, `sessions_restore`,
  `history_search`, `bookmarks_list`, `bookmarks_add`, `bookmarks_update`,
  `bookmarks_remove`, `download` (http/https only, size-capped, approval-
  gated — the `downloads` permission's call site), `cookies_get`,
  `cookies_set`, `cookies_remove`, `inject_js`, `inject_css`, `cdp_eval`,
  `page_screenshot`, `app_screenshot`, `nav_wait` — plus four
  Settings-gated second-tier
  tools that surface once the user enables them:
  `browser_search`, `top_sites`, `reading_list`, `page_capture`.
- Entry points: the side panel, the omnibox (`fa <query>`), the
  Ctrl+Shift+1 hotkey, and the context menu on any selection. Page-derived
  content is quarantined as untrusted data. `inject_js` prompts on every
  call in every session mode by default — explicitly switching the
  session to yolo drops that guard (the override is cleared, not
  bypassed silently).
- Artifact (attached to every release):
  https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/latest/download/fa-extension.zip — unzip, then open
  chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, Load unpacked, pick the
  unzipped folder.
- Architecture and operations: `docs/browser-extension.md` in the repository.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unit tests for the gh-182 ProgramBench leaderboard tooling.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard

Hermetic: the record tests build synthetic _stats dirs in a temp dir and
the render tests feed ledger dicts directly — no test touches the
network (the run/artifact URLs are plain strings by contract).
"""
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import pbench_record
import pbench_render


def _write_stats(stats_dir: Path, score: dict, costs: dict = None,
                 calls: dict = None) -> Path:
    stats_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (stats_dir / "score.json").write_text(json.dumps(score))
    (stats_dir / "cost.json").write_text(json.dumps(costs or {}))
    (stats_dir / "calls.json").write_text(json.dumps(calls or {}))
    return stats_dir


def _ledger_row(**kw) -> dict:
    """A minimal full-run row for render tests."""
    fields = dict(
        taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
        model="kimi-for-coding", mode="full", total=201,
        date="2026-11-02", fa_version="abc123456789",
        run_urls=["https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/500"],
        artifacts=[{"label": "programbench-submission",
                    "url": "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/500/artifacts/42"}],
        instances={
            "cmatrix": {"score_pct": 98.0, "tests": 506, "solved": True,
                        "cost_usd": 0.42, "calls": 57},
        },
    )
    fields.update(kw)
    doc = {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    pbench_record.upsert(doc, **fields)
    return doc


class PbenchRecordTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.ledger = Path(self.tmp.name) / "pbench_results.json"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def _record(self, **kw):
        doc = pbench_record.load_ledger(self.ledger)
        row = pbench_record.upsert(doc, **kw)
        pbench_record.save_ledger(doc, self.ledger)
        return json.loads(self.ledger.read_text())

    def test_seed_row_is_self_reported(self):
        doc = self._record(
            taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
            model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
            date="2026-10-24",
            instances={"cmatrix": {"score_pct": 98.0, "tests": 506,
                                   "solved": True}})
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertTrue(row["self_reported"])
        self.assertEqual(row["mode"], "smoke")
        self.assertEqual(row["attempted"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row["solved"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row["score_pct"], 98.0)
        self.assertEqual(row["taskset_ref"], "895f65916bc5")

    def test_rerun_same_job_updates_not_duplicates(self):
        url = "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/40072410719"
        self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                     model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
                     date="2026-10-24", run_urls=[url],
                     instances={"cmatrix": {"score_pct": 90.0, "tests": 10,
                                            "solved": False}})
        doc = self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                           model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
                           date="2026-10-25", run_urls=[url],
                           instances={"cmatrix": {"score_pct": 98.0,
                                                  "tests": 506,
                                                  "solved": True}})
        self.assertEqual(len(doc["results"]), 1)
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["run_urls"], [url])  # deduped, not doubled
        self.assertEqual(row["date"], "2026-10-25")
        self.assertEqual(row["instances"]["cmatrix"]["score_pct"], 98.0)

    def test_mode_change_is_a_new_row(self):
        # A later full run must NOT overwrite the smoke proof row — the
        # smoke row stays recorded as the pipeline proof it was.
        self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                     model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
                     date="2026-10-24", instances={})
        doc = self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                           model="kimi-for-coding", mode="full", total=201,
                           date="2026-11-02", instances={})
        self.assertEqual(len(doc["results"]), 2)
        self.assertEqual({r["mode"] for r in doc["results"]},
                         {"smoke", "full"})

    def test_multi_run_and_artifact_union(self):
        doc = self._record(
            taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
            model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
            date="2026-10-24",
            run_urls=["https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/1"],
            artifacts=[{"label": "programbench-submission",
                        "url": "https://github.com/o/r/a/1"}])
        doc = self._record(
            taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
            model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
            date="2026-10-25",
            run_urls=["https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/1",
                      "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/2"],
            artifacts=[{"label": "programbench-submission",
                        "url": "https://github.com/o/r/a/2"}])
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["run_urls"], [
            "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/1",
            "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/2"])
        # Same label -> URL updated in place, never duplicated.
        self.assertEqual(row["artifact_urls"], [
            {"label": "programbench-submission",
             "url": "https://github.com/o/r/a/2"}])

    def test_read_stats_parses_score_cost_calls(self):
        stats = _write_stats(
            Path(self.tmp.name) / "_stats",
            score={"cmatrix": {"t/a": True, "t/b": True, "t/c": False},
                   "zip-password-finder": {"t/a": True}},
            costs={"cmatrix": 0.41678, "zip-password-finder": 0.5},
            calls={"cmatrix": 57, "zip-password-finder": 61})
        instances = pbench_record.read_stats(stats)
        self.assertEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["score_pct"], 66.7)
        self.assertEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["tests"], 3)
        self.assertFalse(instances["cmatrix"]["solved"])
        self.assertAlmostEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["cost_usd"], 0.4168)
        self.assertEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["calls"], 57)
        self.assertTrue(instances["zip-password-finder"]["solved"])
        # An instance with calls but no score map still lands (honest
        # gap: rendered as "no score"), never silently dropped.
        self.assertIn("zip-password-finder", instances)

    def test_read_stats_missing_score_json_errors(self):
        with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError):
            pbench_record.read_stats(Path(self.tmp.name) / "nope")

    def test_main_writes_ledger_from_stats_dir(self):
        stats = _write_stats(
            Path(self.tmp.name) / "_stats",
            score={"cmatrix": {"t/a": True, "t/b": True}},
            costs={"cmatrix": 0.25}, calls={"cmatrix": 9})
        rc = pbench_record.main([
            "--ledger", str(self.ledger), "--stats-dir", str(stats),
            "--mode", "smoke", "--model", "kimi-for-coding",
            "--pbench-version", "1.2.5", "--taskset-ref", "895f65916bc5",
            "--total", "201", "--fa-version", "abc123456789",
            "--date", "2026-10-24",
            "--run-url", "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/7",
            "--artifact",
            "programbench-submission=https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/7/artifacts/42",
        ])
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        row = json.loads(self.ledger.read_text())["results"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["mode"], "smoke")
        self.assertEqual(row["attempted"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row["cost_usd"], 0.25)
        self.assertEqual(row["calls"], 9)
        self.assertEqual(row["artifact_urls"][0]["label"],
                         "programbench-submission")

    def test_main_rejects_unknown_mode(self):
        rc = pbench_record.main([
            "--ledger", str(self.ledger),
            "--stats-dir", str(Path(self.tmp.name)),
            "--mode", "yolo", "--model", "m",
            "--taskset-ref", "r", "--total", "201",
        ])
        self.assertEqual(rc, 2)

    def test_main_rejects_malformed_artifact(self):
        rc = pbench_record.main([
            "--ledger", str(self.ledger),
            "--stats-dir", str(Path(self.tmp.name)),
            "--mode", "smoke", "--model", "m",
            "--taskset-ref", "r", "--total", "201",
            "--artifact", "no-equals-sign",
        ])
        self.assertEqual(rc, 2)


class PbenchRenderTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def _smoke_ledger(self) -> dict:
        return _ledger_row(
            mode="smoke", date="2026-10-24", fa_version=None,
            run_urls=["https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/40072410719"],
            artifacts=[],
            instances={
                "cmatrix": {"score_pct": 98.0, "tests": 506, "solved": True},
                "zip-password-finder": {"score_pct": 98.0, "tests": 680,
                                        "solved": True},
            })

    def test_smoke_row_is_marked_pipeline_proof(self):
        section = pbench_render.render_section(self._smoke_ledger())
        self.assertIn("pipeline proof", section)
        self.assertIn("not a leaderboard row", section.lower())
        self.assertIn("2 of 201", section)
        self.assertIn("⭐ kimi-for-coding", section)
        self.assertIn("self-reported", section.lower())
        # Honesty contract: never reads as an official submission.
        self.assertIn("never auto-submitted", section)

    def test_full_row_sorts_above_smoke(self):
        doc = self._smoke_ledger()
        pbench_record.upsert(
            doc, taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
            model="glm-5.3-flash", mode="full", total=201,
            date="2026-11-02", instances={})
        section = pbench_render.render_section(doc)
        # The headline-worthy full row comes first even though the smoke
        # row was recorded first.
        self.assertLess(section.index("⭐ glm-5.3-flash"),
                        section.index("⭐ kimi-for-coding"))

    def test_run_and_artifact_links_render(self):
        doc = _ledger_row()
        section = pbench_render.render_section(doc)
        self.assertIn(
            "[500](https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/500)", section)
        self.assertIn(
            "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/500/artifacts/42", section)
        # Per-instance detail: score, tests, solved, cost, calls.
        self.assertIn("| cmatrix | 98.0% | 506 | ✅ | $0.42 | 57 |", section)

    def test_missing_artifacts_fall_back_to_run_link(self):
        section = pbench_render.render_section(self._smoke_ledger())
        self.assertIn("see the run page", section.lower())
        self.assertIn(
            "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/40072410719", section)

    def test_splice_roundtrip_and_idempotency(self):
        section = pbench_render.render_section(self._smoke_ledger())
        text = ("<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->\n\n"
                "## What's inside\n\nbody\n")
        once = pbench_render.splice_readme(text, section)
        self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN, once)
        self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_END, once)
        # Inserted after the Terminal-Bench region, before the anchor
        # heading, which survives.
        self.assertLess(once.index("<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->"),
                        once.index(pbench_render.SECTION_HEADER))
        self.assertLess(once.index(pbench_render.SECTION_HEADER),
                        once.index("## What's inside"))
        # A second splice replaces — no duplicated blocks.
        twice = pbench_render.splice_readme(once, section)
        self.assertEqual(once.count(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN), 1)
        self.assertEqual(twice, once)

    def test_splice_without_anchor_inserts_before_heading(self):
        section = pbench_render.render_section(self._smoke_ledger())
        out = pbench_render.splice_readme("# Only a title\n", section)
        self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN, out)

    def test_html_page_renders_same_block(self):
        html = pbench_render.render_html(self._smoke_ledger())
        self.assertIn("<!doctype html>", html.lower())
        self.assertIn("ProgramBench", html)
        self.assertIn("pipeline proof", html)
        self.assertIn("2 of 201", html)
        self.assertIn("⭐ kimi-for-coding", html)
        self.assertIn("https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/40072410719", html)
        # Instance ids are machine data — never interpolated raw.
        self.assertNotIn("<cmatrix>", html)

    def test_html_escapes_instance_ids(self):
        doc = _ledger_row(instances={
            "<script>alert(1)</script>": {"score_pct": 50.0, "tests": 2,
                                          "solved": False},
        })
        html = pbench_render.render_html(doc)
        self.assertNotIn("<script>alert(1)</script>", html)
        self.assertIn("<script>", html)

    def test_main_writes_readme_and_html_and_check(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            readme = Path(tmp) / "README.md"
            readme.write_text(
                "<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->\n\n"
                "## What's inside\n\nbody\n")
            html = Path(tmp) / "programbench.html"
            ledger = Path(tmp) / "pbench_results.json"
            ledger.write_text(json.dumps(self._smoke_ledger()))
            argv = ["--readme", str(readme), "--ledger", str(ledger),
                    "--html", str(html)]
            self.assertEqual(pbench_render.main(argv + ["--check"]), 1)
            self.assertEqual(pbench_render.main(argv), 0)
            self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN, readme.read_text())
            self.assertIn("pipeline proof", html.read_text())
            # Second run is a no-op (idempotent), --check agrees.
            self.assertEqual(pbench_render.main(argv + ["--check"]), 0)

    def test_main_requires_a_surface(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            ledger = Path(tmp) / "pbench_results.json"
            ledger.write_text(json.dumps({"schema": 1, "results": []}))
            self.assertEqual(
                pbench_render.main(["--ledger", str(ledger)]), 2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ProgramBench results ledger upsert (gh-182).

`bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json` is the committed ledger of fa's
OWN ProgramBench results — per-instance score/tests, cost, calls,
provider/model, run id + artifact links, and the smoke|lite|full mode —
the `fa_results.json` pattern applied to bench-programbench.yml. It is
written by the bench-programbench.yml aggregate step on every GREEN run
(summary verdict + Tier-0 `submit verify` passed) and by hand for
backfills (the seed smoke row was recorded this way).

Usage:

    pbench_record.py --stats-dir pbench-run/<RUN_ID>/_stats \
        --taskset-ref 895f65916bc5 --pbench-version 1.2.5 \
        --model kimi-for-coding --mode smoke --total 201 \
        [--fa-version 2fd100169e] [--date 2026-10-24] \
        [--run-url https://github.com/.../actions/runs/40072410719]... \
        [--artifact "programbench-submission=<url>"]...

`--stats-dir` is the merged run dir's `_stats/` written by `programbench
submit package` + summary.py: score.json (the per-instance
{branch/test: bool} map), cost.json + calls.json (self-reported, from
the fa session logs). Score pct = share of that instance's scored tests
that passed; solved = every scored test true (summary.py's ✅
convention).

Idempotency contract: rows are keyed by (taskset_ref, model, mode) —
one row per task-set pin x model x mode. Re-recording the same job
updates numbers/dates in place and unions run_urls / artifact_urls
(same label -> URL updated); it never appends a duplicate row. A mode
change (smoke -> full) is a NEW row: the smoke proof (attempted << the
official total) must survive next to the headline run, never be
overwritten by it. Renders (pbench_render.py) sort full runs first and
label smoke rows as pipeline proofs — a smoke result is never presented
as a leaderboard headline.

Every row is self-reported evidence: `self_reported: true` is set by
this tool. Nothing here writes the official ProgramBench registry —
submission stays a manual self-serve PR decision by the owner
(docs/bench.md).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("pbench_results.json")

# The closed dispatch-mode set — tasks.py's `_select` outputs (the
# workflow's setup `mode` output). Unknown modes fail here instead of
# rendering as an unlabeled row.
MODES = ("smoke", "lite", "globs", "full")


def load_ledger(path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    doc.setdefault("results", [])
    return doc


def save_ledger(doc: dict, path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")


def _key(row: dict) -> "tuple[str, str, str]":
    return (row.get("taskset_ref", ""), row.get("model", ""),
            row.get("mode", ""))


def read_stats(stats_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """Per-instance entries from the packaged `_stats/` maps.

    score.json is the required input (a green aggregate always has it —
    the verdict gate fails the run before record is reached otherwise);
    cost.json/calls.json entries ride along when present. An instance
    known only from cost/calls still lands with no score fields — a gap
    must render as "no score", never silently disappear.
    """
    score_path = stats_dir / "score.json"
    score = json.loads(score_path.read_text()) if score_path.is_file() else None
    if score is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no score.json under {stats_dir} — "
                                "record runs only after `programbench "
                                "submit package`")
    costs = json.loads((stats_dir / "cost.json").read_text()) \
        if (stats_dir / "cost.json").is_file() else {}
    calls = json.loads((stats_dir / "calls.json").read_text()) \
        if (stats_dir / "calls.json").is_file() else {}

    instances: dict = {}
    for iid in sorted(set(score) | set(costs) | set(calls)):
        entry: dict = {}
        tests = score.get(iid)
        if isinstance(tests, dict) and tests:
            passed = sum(1 for v in tests.values() if v is True)
            entry["score_pct"] = round(100.0 * passed / len(tests), 1)
            entry["tests"] = len(tests)
            entry["solved"] = passed == len(tests)
        if iid in costs:
            entry["cost_usd"] = round(float(costs[iid]), 4)
        if iid in calls:
            entry["calls"] = int(calls[iid])
        instances[iid] = entry
    return instances


def upsert(doc: dict, *, taskset_ref: str, model: str, mode: str, total: int,
           instances: dict, date: str = None, pbench_version: str = None,
           fa_version: str = None, run_urls: "list[str]" = (),
           artifacts: "list[dict]" = ()) -> dict:
    """Insert or update the (taskset_ref, model, mode) row.

    Existing run_urls are unioned (sorted, deduped) and artifact_urls
    merged by label so a job re-run updates instead of duplicating;
    numbers/date reflect the latest record call.
    """
    if mode not in MODES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown mode {mode!r} — expected one of "
                         f"{', '.join(MODES)} (tasks.py's output set)")
    row = None
    for existing in doc["results"]:
        if _key(existing) == (taskset_ref, model, mode):
            row = existing
            break
    if row is None:
        row = {"taskset_ref": taskset_ref, "model": model, "mode": mode}
        doc["results"].append(row)

    urls = set(row.get("run_urls") or [])
    urls.update(u for u in run_urls if u)
    by_label = {a["label"]: a["url"] for a in row.get("artifact_urls") or []}
    for a in artifacts or ():
        if a.get("label") and a.get("url"):
            by_label[a["label"]] = a["url"]

    scores = [e["score_pct"] for e in instances.values()
              if isinstance(e.get("score_pct"), (int, float))]
    costs = [e["cost_usd"] for e in instances.values()
             if isinstance(e.get("cost_usd"), (int, float))]
    calls = [e["calls"] for e in instances.values()
             if isinstance(e.get("calls"), int)]

    row.update(
        {
            "date": date or datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat(),
            "total": int(total),
            "attempted": len(instances),
            "solved": sum(1 for e in instances.values()
                          if e.get("solved") is True),
            "instances": dict(sorted(instances.items())),
            "run_urls": sorted(urls),
            "artifact_urls": [{"label": k, "url": by_label[k]}
                              for k in sorted(by_label)],
            # fa rows are self-reported, never official (gh-182 R4).
            "self_reported": True,
        }
    )
    row["score_pct"] = round(sum(scores) / len(scores), 1) if scores else None
    row["cost_usd"] = round(sum(costs), 4) if costs else None
    row["calls"] = sum(calls) if calls else None
    if pbench_version:
        row["pbench_version"] = pbench_version
    if fa_version:
        row["fa_version"] = fa_version
    # Stable order: task-set pin, then model, then mode — deterministic
    # for merges; the renderer applies its own presentation order.
    doc["results"].sort(key=_key)
    return row


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=LEDGER_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--stats-dir", type=Path, required=True,
                        help="merged run dir's _stats/ (score/cost/calls)")
    parser.add_argument("--taskset-ref", dest="taskset_ref", required=True,
                        help="facebookresearch/ProgramBench pin (short sha)")
    parser.add_argument("--pbench-version", dest="pbench_version",
                        help="PyPI programbench pin the run evaluated with")
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True,
                        help="provider model id (the resolved bench_model)")
    parser.add_argument("--mode", required=True, choices=MODES,
                        help="dispatch mode from tasks.py (smoke/lite/"
                             "globs/full)")
    parser.add_argument("--total", type=int, required=True,
                        help="FULL official instance count (the dilution "
                             "denominator; tasks.py's `total` output)")
    parser.add_argument("--date",
                        help="run date YYYY-MM-DD (default: today UTC)")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-version", dest="fa_version",
                        help="fa ref the run executed")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_urls", action="append",
                        default=[])

arguments.newText:
# The one-step handoff artifact: exactly the folder docs/bench.md
      # tells a maintainer to publish + PR to ProgramBench/submissions.
      - name: Upload submission folder
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: programbench-submission
          path: pbench-run/

      # gh-182: resolve the submission artifact's download link (the run
      # dir: trajectories, eval logs, _stats — the post-run analysis
      # surface). Best-effort: an API hiccup degrades to the run-page
      # fallback the renderer already speaks; it must never flip a green
      # aggregate red.
      - name: Resolve artifact link
        id: artifact
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          artifact_url=""
          if id=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/artifacts" \
              --jq '.artifacts[] | select(.name=="programbench-submission") | .id' 2>/dev/null | head -1) \
              && [ -n "$id" ]; then
            artifact_url="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/artifacts/$id"
          fi
          {
            echo "artifact_url=$artifact_url"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # gh-182: append the run to the committed ProgramBench ledger
      # (bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json — the fa_results.json
      # pattern: keyed by task-set pin x model x mode, run/artifact URLs
      # unioned, idempotent) and regenerate the README section next to
      # the Terminal-Bench one. Runs only on a GREEN aggregate (the
      # verdict + Tier-0 verify steps passed) — a partial or failing run
      # never lands. Smoke/lite/globs runs record too, and the renderer
      # labels them pipeline proofs — never a leaderboard headline. The
      # official ProgramBench registry is NOT touched (manual owner PR).
      - name: Update ProgramBench ledger & README
        if: success()
        env:
          MODE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.mode }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          TOTAL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.total }}
          PB_REF: ${{ inputs.programbench-ref }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          ARTIFACT_URL: ${{ steps.artifact.outputs.artifact_url }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          record_args=(--ledger bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json
            --stats-dir "pbench-run/$RUN_ID/_stats"
            --taskset-ref "${PB_REF:0:12}"
            --pbench-version "$PB_VERSION"
            --mode "$MODE" --model "$MODEL" --total "$TOTAL"
            --fa-version "${FA_REF:0:12}" --date "$(date -u +%F)"
            --run-url "$RUN_URL")
          if [ -n "$ARTIFACT_URL" ]; then
            record_args+=(--artifact "programbench-submission=$ARTIFACT_URL")
          fi
          python bench/leaderboard/pbench_record.py "${record_args[@]}"
          python bench/leaderboard/pbench_render.py \
            --readme README.md \
            --ledger bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add README.md bench/leaderboard
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "pbench leaderboard: ledger and table already up to date"
          else
            git commit -m "bench: programbench ledger update · ${MODE} · ${MODEL} (gh-182)"
            git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
          fi

## Project

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness)
- [pub.dev package](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_agent_harness)
- [Issue tracker](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues)

## Key facts

- Written in Dart; the core library is pure Dart (no dart:io) and compiles to web.
- Providers: OpenAI-compatible (incl. OpenRouter and Ollama Cloud), Anthropic, Google.
- Web sandbox is a pure-Dart in-memory shell; mobile uses WASI binaries
  (uutils coreutils, ripgrep, sed/awk, python3, sqlite3, lua) under an embedded
  wasm runtime.
- Ships as: CLI (`fa`/`fah`), Flutter apps (iOS/Android/macOS/Windows/Linux),
  a static web app, a Chrome MV3 extension, and an Outlook Office add-in.
- License: MIT. Published on pub.dev as `flutter_agent_harness`.

## FAQ (quotable answers)

- name: Upload submission folder
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: programbench-submission
          path: pbench-run/

      # gh-182: resolve the submission artifact's download link (the run
      # dir: trajectories, eval logs, _stats — the post-run analysis
      # surface). Best-effort: an API hiccup degrades to the run-page
      # fallback the renderer already speaks; it must never flip a green
      # aggregate red.
      - name: Resolve artifact link
        id: artifact
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          artifact_url=""
          if id=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/artifacts" \
              --jq '.artifacts[] | select(.name=="programbench-submission") | .id' 2>/dev/null | head -1) \
              && [ -n "$id" ]; then
            artifact_url="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/artifacts/$id"
          fi
          {
            echo "artifact_url=$artifact_url"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # gh-182: append the run to the committed ProgramBench ledger
      # (bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json — the fa_results.json
      # pattern: keyed by task-set pin x model x mode, run/artifact URLs
      # unioned, idempotent) and regenerate the README section next to
      # the Terminal-Bench one. Runs only on a GREEN aggregate (the
      # verdict + Tier-0 verify steps passed) — a partial or failing run
      # never lands. Smoke/lite/globs runs record too, and the renderer
      # labels them pipeline proofs — never a leaderboard headline. The
      # official ProgramBench registry is NOT touched (manual owner PR).
      - name: Update ProgramBench ledger & README
        if: success()
        env:
          MODE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.mode }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          TOTAL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.total }}
          PB_REF: ${{ inputs.programbench-ref }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          ARTIFACT_URL: ${{ steps.artifact.outputs.artifact_url }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          record_args=(--ledger bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json
            --stats-dir "pbench-run/$RUN_ID/_stats"
            --taskset-ref "${PB_REF:0:12}"
            --pbench-version "$PB_VERSION"
            --mode "$MODE" --model "$MODEL" --total "$TOTAL"
            --fa-version "${FA_REF:0:12}" --date "$(date -u +%F)"
            --run-url "$RUN_URL")
          if [ -n "$ARTIFACT_URL" ]; then
            record_args+=(--artifact "programbench-submission=$ARTIFACT_URL")
          fi
          python bench/leaderboard/pbench_record.py "${record_args[@]}"
          python bench/leaderboard/pbench_render.py \
            --readme README.md \
            --ledger bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add README.md bench/leaderboard
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "pbench leaderboard: ledger and table already up to date"
          else
            git commit -m "bench: programbench ledger update · ${MODE} · ${MODEL} (gh-182)"
            git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
          fi

### What changed ProgramBench results now survive the CI artifact window: the `bench-programbench` aggregate job records every green run into a committed ledger (`bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json` — the `fa_results.json` pattern, keyed by task-set pin × model × mode) and regenerates a README ProgramBench section next to the Terminal-Bench one; `pages.yml` renders the same block as `fa1.dev/programbench.html` with run + analysis-artifact links. ### Key decisions - Sibling tooling, not edits to the gh-1682 files: `pbench_record.py` (ledger upsert, reads `_stats/{score,cost,calls}.json`) and `pbench_render.py` (one renderer → README marked region + standalone HTML page, deterministic — no clock/network). - Smoke/lite/globs runs record too, but the renderer sorts full runs first and labels smoke rows `pipeline proof (2 of 201), not a leaderboard row` — never a headline; a mode change is a new row, so a later full run never overwrites the proof. - Artifact links: the aggregate resolves the `programbench-submission` artifact id via the Actions API (job gains `actions: read`); on API failure the renderer falls back to an explicit "see the run page" link instead of a dead one. Trajectories + eval logs ride that artifact. - No official-registry submission anywhere (manual owner PR unchanged). - Seeded the ledger with the smoke run 40023718645 (kimi-for-coding: cmatrix 98% / 506 tests, zip-password-finder 98% / 680 tests) per the ledger's backfill contract. - `pages.yml` gains a `bench/leaderboard/**` paths trigger so an aggregate push redeploys fa1.dev; landing nav/footer + `llms.txt` link the page. ### How to verify ```bash python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard # 40 tests, hermetic (19 new) python3 bench/leaderboard/pbench_render.py --readme README.md --ledger bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json --check ```
Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[bench-programbench aggregate
verdict + Tier-0 verify green] --> B[resolve artifact id
gh api actions:read] B --> C[pbench_record.py
_stats → pbench_results.json] C --> D[pbench_render.py
README section] D --> E[commit + push main] E --> F[pages.yml paths trigger] F --> G[fa1.dev/programbench.html] ```
